title: Finite separability makes the differential of a smooth curve map nonzero
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Y$ be curves over $k$, meaning separated integral schemes of finite type and dimension one [def-pc-curve], and suppose both are smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a dominant $k$-morphism (its image is dense in $Y$), with induced finite separable extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ of function fields [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-tower]. Write $\Omega_{Z/k}$ for the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Then the canonical map
$$\mathrm df:f^*\Omega_{Y/k}\longrightarrow\Omega_{X/k}$$
[def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map], with module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], is nonzero.

proof.text: Put $K=k(Y)$ and $L=k(X)$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-generic-differentials] to each smooth curve. We obtain the germ-normalized isomorphisms $\alpha_Y:(\Omega_{Y/k})_{\eta_Y}\cong\Omega_{K/k}$ and $\alpha_X:(\Omega_{X/k})_{\eta_X}\cong\Omega_{L/k}$. Their targets have dimension one; in particular $\Omega_{L/k}\ne0$.

Apply [lem-sfb-dominant-generic-differential-comparison] to $f$ and these two isomorphisms. Its hypotheses require only integrality, dominance and their formula on germs, all supplied above. It sends $\eta_X$ to $\eta_Y$ and identifies the function-field map with the induced stalk map $\varphi:K\to L$. Its isomorphism $\beta_f$ identifies $\alpha_X\circ(df)_{\eta_X}\circ\beta_f^{-1}$ with $T:L\otimes_K\Omega_{K/k}\to\Omega_{L/k}$, $a\otimes db\mapsto a\,d\varphi(b)$.

The given finite separable extension is this induced $L/K$. For the field tower $k\to K\to L$, [lem-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-differentials-base-change] says exactly that $T$ is an isomorphism. Since its target is nonzero, choose a nonzero vector $v$ there: $T(T^{-1}v)=v\ne0$. Thus $T$ and, by the two coordinate isomorphisms, $(df)_{\eta_X}$ are nonzero.

proof.text: By the germ formula in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], a sheaf morphism $u$ acts by $u_x(s_x)=u(s)_x$. If $df=0$, this is the zero map at every point, since the image of every section is zero; in particular $(df)_{\eta_X}=0$. This contradicts Step 3. Therefore $df\ne0$.
